### What does this PR do?

`trainer.v1.trainer_mode=group_delivery` runs rollout and Megatron training on **disaggregated** GPU pools (`actor_rollout_ref.hybrid_engine=False`), which is where the long tail of agentic rollouts otherwise leaves the training pool idle. This PR turns that topology into an overlap: a complete GRPO group is forwarded and backwarded as soon as its own responses and rewards arrive, while the remaining prompts of the fixed batch are still generating. Execution is therefore asynchronous; the policy update is not. Actor parameters stay unchanged until every group in the original batch has contributed gradients; then there is one optimizer step, one scheduler step and one weight sync before the next batch is submitted, so the update is exactly batch-synchronous (zero staleness).

Unlike `separate_async`, the actor is never updated per mini-batch and no trajectory is consumed under an older policy version; unlike a fully asynchronous trainer, there is a fixed batch boundary. The schedule is asynchronous in execution, synchronous in policy updates.

This is the same observation that motivates gradient streaming in [ThunderSyncRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05935): once a trajectory's inputs (here a complete GRPO group) are fixed, its backward can be released early without changing the update. Prior asynchronous trainers ([PipelineRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19128), [StreamRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15930), [AReaL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24298)) recover utilization by allowing policy lag; this PR keeps zero lag and instead removes the idle time inside one batch.

The effect is higher training-pool utilization and lower end-to-end time, and the gain grows with the spread of group completion times. On a long-CoT workload (AReaL-boba math, Qwen3-1.7B, 8192-token responses, 100 steps) with the same disaggregated 2 training + 1 rollout GPU allocation, data order and seed, the median step time is 18.2% lower and wall time 11.2% lower than the full-batch barrier (`wait_for_full_batch=True`). The benefit comes from long-tailed rollouts: as the tail shrinks, the schedule converges to the barrier.

Related PRs: #8203 streams the dataloader for the V1 sync PPO trainer (complementary; this PR keeps a fixed batch and streams per-group gradient work). #6868 adds a streaming-rollouter mode to the V1 trainer and does not overlap with the per-group gradient path.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Query links:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22group+delivery%22
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+per-group+backward
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+long-tail+rollout
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`

### Test

Unit and lint (CPU):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/workers/test_group_gradient_accumulator_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_group_delivery_worker_on_cpu.py -q
# 33 passed

pre-commit run --files <the 8 changed files>
# all hooks passed
```

End-to-end (single node, 3×A6000 48 GB). Both arms use the same disaggregated allocation (2 training GPUs, 1 rollout GPU), the same data order and seed, and 100 steps; warmup steps 1–2 are excluded.

**Table 1 — end-to-end.**

| workload | mode | wall (h) | step median (s) | step P95 (s) | throughput (tok/s/GPU) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-1.7B, AReaL-boba math, 8192-token CoT | `group_delivery` | **1.621** | **44.9** | **118.5** | **121.6** |
| same | `wait_for_full_batch=True` | 1.826 | 54.9 | 130.5 | 99.8 |

**Table 2 — scheduling and utilization.**

| metric | `group_delivery` | `wait_for_full_batch=True` |
|---|---:|---:|
| group latency P50 / P95 / P99 (s) | 16.4 / 72.9 / 104.0 | 39.2 / 96.0 / 123.2 |
| overlapped groups per batch | 2.43 | 0 |
| training GPU mean utilization | 36.8% / 36.9% | 30.7% / 31.0% |
| rollout GPU mean utilization | 66.4% | 57.9% |
| allocated / active GPU-hours | 4.861 / 2.636 | 5.476 / 2.535 |
| actor update mean (s) | 19.75 | 18.80 |
| weight sync mean (s) | 1.63 | 1.62 |

The tail is real generation-length variance, not injected delay: per-group latency P50 16.4 s / P95 72.9 s (P95/P50 4.5) in the trainer, and P95/P50 6.9 over 128 raw samples from the same engine. Rewards stay flat because AReaL-boba is hard for a 1.7B model; the tables measure scheduling, not learning. The ~1 s higher actor update is the per-group schedule overhead plus the host-resident accumulator (see Design).

### API and Usage Example

```bash
python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  trainer.v1.trainer_mode=group_delivery \
  actor_rollout_ref.hybrid_engine=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n_gpus_per_node=1 \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=2 \
  trainer.v1.group_delivery.wait_for_full_batch=False   # True = full-batch barrier
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Per-group delivery and gradient accumulation: the controller forwards one complete GRPO group to all actor ranks while the rollout pool keeps generating. Padding uses synthetic sequences with zero response masks, so one group can be delivered even when its response count is smaller than the DP size, and all ranks execute the same collective sequence. - `utils/metric/utils.py`: aggregate a DP all-gathered `list[Metric]` before reducing.
- `examples/group_delivery/`: the example tool environment serializes environment access process-wide (the shared text-world parser is not thread-safe), emits episode records on stdout, and exposes optional deterministic slow-task knobs for tail experiments.

- [x] Read the Contribute Guide.
- [x] Run pre-commit on the changed files.
- [ ] Add / update documentation. `docs/advance/group_delivery.md` already describes the mode and the `wait_for_full_batch` control; this PR does not change the user-facing contract, and the experiment notes live in `artifacts/group_delivery/NOTES.md` (not part of this branch).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_host_resident_sums_match_device_resident_sums` covers the host-resident accumulator path; the existing group-delivery worker tests cover delivery, padding and the optimizer barrier.
- [ ] CI request in Slack (`ci-request`): pending.
- [ ] `recipe` submodule: not applicable.

### References

- ThunderSyncRL: *Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning*, arXiv [2610.05935](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05935) — gradient streaming once an objective source's inputs are fixed, zero staleness; up to 1.9× on long-tailed SWE runs.

+# Synchronous GRPO with group delivery
+
+Last updated: 10/27/2026.
+
+`trainer.v1.trainer_mode=group_delivery` runs rollout and Megatron training on
+separate GPU pools. It submits one fixed batch of prompts under policy version
+`k`. Once all responses and rewards for a prompt are available, that complete
+GRPO group runs forward/backward while other prompts are still generating.
+Actor parameters remain unchanged until **every group in the original batch**
+has contributed gradients. Then there is one optimizer step, one scheduler step,
+and one weight synchronization before the next batch is submitted.
+
+This differs from `separate_async`, which updates the actor per mini-batch and
+can consume older policy versions. `group_delivery` does not prefetch next-step
+prompts, refill failed groups, drop slow groups, or resume partially generated
+trajectories across policy versions.
+
+## Configuration
+
+Use the standard `verl.trainer.main_ppo` entry point with these overrides:
+
+```bash
+model_engine=megatron \
+trainer.v1.trainer_mode=group_delivery \
+actor_rollout_ref.hybrid_engine=False \
+algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
+data.train_batch_size=64 \
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=64 \
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_epochs=1 \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=8 \
+actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
+actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.nnodes=1 \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n_gpus_per_node=8 \
+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend=nccl
+```
+
+Set `trainer.nnodes` and `trainer.n_gpus_per_node` for the training pool, and
+configure the dataset, model, rollout backend and parallel topology as usual.
+The rollout pool is additional to the training pool. Polling for completed
+groups defaults to 50 ms (`trainer.v1.group_delivery.poll_interval`).
+
+`tests/special_e2e/run_v1_group_delivery.sh` is a three-GPU, two-step ALFWorld
+launcher (two training GPUs and one rollout GPU). It takes `MODEL_PATH` and
+`DATA_DIR` from the environment. See the [A6000 handoff](group_delivery_handoff.md)
+for environment setup, the measured long-tail workload and acceptance commands.
+
+For an overlap ablation, `trainer.v1.group_delivery.wait_for_full_batch=True`
+holds delivery until every original group is ready, then uses the same worker
+and per-group gradient accumulation. It is a measurement control, not another
+training algorithm. Default: `False`.
+
+## Gradient and failure semantics
+
+The controller forwards one complete prompt group to all actor ranks at a time.
+DP padding uses synthetic sequences with zero response masks. This allows a
+single group to be delivered even when its response count is smaller than DP
+size. All ranks execute the same collective sequence; they do not consume
+independent queues. Small groups can still incur poor pipeline utilization.
+
+Megatron's pipeline schedule finalizes its gradients after each call, including
+DP reduce-scatter and, in some configurations, per-token gradient scaling.
+Keeping old gradients in those buffers would process them again on the next
+call. Instead, the worker copies each group's finalized gradients to a separate
+FP32 accumulator and resets the schedule buffers. After all groups arrive, it
+restores the weighted global mean directly to the native buffers and invokes the
+optimizer. Gradient clipping and the scheduler run only at this final boundary.
+
+For `token-mean`, group gradients are weighted by the group's valid response-token
+count and divided by the whole batch's token count. For sequence means, the
+weights are valid sequence counts. Consequently, short groups do not receive the
+same weight as long groups under a token-mean objective. Padding is excluded from
+both normalizers. The implementation costs one additional FP32 gradient buffer
+and performs gradient communication per group; it prioritizes correctness over
+minimizing communication.
+
+If rollout or backward fails, the batch fails without an optimizer update. A
+failed group is not replaced by a new prompt. Foreign, duplicate, incomplete,
+and wrong-version groups are rejected. At training step `k`, each trajectory
+must report prompt step `k` and both rollout weight-version bounds equal to `k-1`.
+Checkpoints are taken only after the full update; mid-accumulation recovery is not supported. Restore from the previous
+completed checkpoint after a failed run. An async checkpoint containing pending
+prompt groups cannot be resumed in this mode.
+
+## Supported scope
+
+The initial implementation supports standard GRPO with vanilla PPO loss, one
+epoch and one optimizer step per rollout batch. Token means, sequence means,
+entropy regularization, reference-policy KL loss, TP, PP, static CP and native
+Megatron DDP/distributed optimizer use the existing engine collectives. These
+GPU paths have regression scripts but have not been run on the CPU development
+machine; they require the acceptance matrix in the handoff. Rollout log probabilities or
+recomputed old log probabilities can be used; actor weights are fixed for both.
+
+The following combinations are rejected rather than silently changing the
+objective:
+
+- Non-Megatron backends, FP16, non-FP32 gradient buffers, Megatron FSDP,
+  precision-aware optimizers, quantized training, parameter/optimizer offload, dynamic CP and VPP.
+- MTP, nonzero MoE auxiliary/z losses, expert-bias updates, quantile balancing and Sinkhorn routing.
+  MoE models with these features disabled can use ordinary expert parallelism.
+- Critic training, distillation, KL-in-reward, batch-dependent policy losses,
+  rollout importance/rejection correction, score centering, dynamic group
+  filtering, custom samplers and rollout skipping.
+- Variable `rollout.n` and multiple output trajectories per agent session.
+  Ordinary multi-turn sessions returning one final trajectory are supported.
+
+`seq-mean-token-sum-norm` additionally requires a positive, fixed
+`actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_scale_factor`. Group-local maximum sequence lengths
+must not change the normalization of this objective.
+
+## Verification
+
+```bash
+pytest -q tests/workers/test_group_gradient_accumulator_on_cpu.py \
+  tests/workers/test_group_delivery_worker_on_cpu.py \
+  tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_group_delivery_on_cpu.py \
+  tests/special_standalone/test_group_delivery_alfworld_on_cpu.py
+```
+
+The numerical tests compare a single full-batch GRPO-style update with streaming
+groups of unequal response lengths and different completion orders. They check
+the accumulated gradient, clipped gradient norm and AdamW parameter update.
+Controller tests check that a ready group is consumed while another is still
+running and that failures cannot commit a partial batch.
+
+GPU acceptance includes `tests/models/test_group_delivery_megatron.py`, which
+uses a tiny locally generated Qwen3 model, fixed responses, the real Megatron
+optimizer and two consecutive steps. It compares owned FP32 gradient shards,
+clipped gradient norms and optimizer updates for whole-batch versus delivered
+groups. The matrix includes DP, TP, PP, CP, combinations and groups smaller than
+DP. Cases requiring more GPUs than are visible are explicitly skipped.
+
+`group_delivery_event` log records mark batch begin, group backward begin/end,
+optimizer begin/end and weight sync begin/end. A backward begin with
+`pending_groups > 0` is evidence of actual overlap. The metric
+`training/groups_backward_started_during_rollout` counts such groups per batch.
+
+The Megatron per-token loss path also preserves the remainder when distributing
+real token counts across static CP ranks. Truncating every rank's share would
+make the final gradient divisor depend on group/micro-batch boundaries.
+
+## Relationship to existing work
+
+This mode reuses the upstream Tinker split primitives, standalone rollout setup,
+TransferQueue, GRPO advantage computation, token packing and Megatron schedules.
+Its addition is the fixed-batch delivery/commit protocol and finalized-gradient
+accumulator. The public PR audit and remaining GPU validation are recorded in
+[the handoff](group_delivery_handoff.md).

+## 训练语义和支持边界
+
+每次 Megatron schedule 都会 finalize 梯度。直接把上一组梯度留在 native buffer 中，可能重复归约或缩放。
+这里将每组 finalize 后的梯度拷到额外 FP32 accumulator，再清空 native buffer。
+最后把整批加权平均写回，交给原生 optimizer 做全局 norm、clip 和 update。
+`token-mean` 按有效 response token 数加权；sequence mean 按至少有一个有效 response token 的样本数加权。
+工具观察与 padding 不计入有效 response token。
+
+所有 DP/TP/PP/CP rank 按同一 group 顺序进入 collective。DP lane 不够时补零 loss 的样本，
+不能让不同 DP rank 各自从队列取不同 group。TP/PP/静态 CP 与组合沿用 Megatron 的 process groups。
+actor/reference 的 DP 对齐分别计算；同进程的 Megatron actor/reference 仍须遵循上游共享 model-parallel
+初始化的限制，不能据此配置两个独立的 TP/PP/CP 拓扑。通信发生在每组，额外内存约为一份本 rank 原生 FP32 梯度 buffer；
+所以小 group、通信瓶颈或 PP 空泡可能抵消 rollout 重叠收益，不能预先承诺加速。
+
+当前限定：BF16、原生 Megatron DDP/普通 Adam 或 SGD、GRPO、vanilla PPO loss、`ppo_epochs=1`、
+`ppo_mini_batch_size=train_batch_size`。支持 token/sequence mean、熵正则及 reference KL loss。
+`seq-mean-token-sum-norm` 必须指定固定正 `loss_scale_factor`。

+以下组合会拒绝启动：动态 CP、VPP、Megatron FSDP、precision-aware optimizer、参数/optimizer offload、
+FP8/FP4/QAT、MTP、非零 MoE aux/z loss、expert bias/quantile 状态更新、Sinkhorn、critic、distillation、

+人工结束环境服务的失败注入应让训练失败且没有本批 optimizer_end；从上一完整 checkpoint 能继续。
+
+独立做一次 checkpoint 恢复：把两步 smoke 的 `global_step_2` 路径传给
+`trainer.resume_mode=resume_path trainer.resume_from_path=... trainer.total_training_steps=3`。
+恢复后第 3 步只消费新 batch，没有旧 prompt 遗留。性能测试关闭保存，避免 checkpoint 时间干扰。
+
+## 重叠收益的对照实验
+
+先用 DP2。相同模型、数据文件、batch、n、seed、并发、截断、GPU 分配，分别跑：
+
+```bash
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2 bash tests/special_e2e/run_v1_group_delivery.sh \

+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import time
+
+import httpx
+
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.agent_loop import ToolListWrap
+from verl.experimental.agent_loop.tool_agent_loop import AgentState, ToolAgentLoop
+from verl.tools.base_tool import BaseTool
+from verl.tools.schemas import OpenAIFunctionToolSchema, ToolResponse
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
+
+
+def server_url():
+    """Use a separately installed CPU environment service on the same machine."""
+    return os.environ.get("ALFWORLD_SERVER_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765").rstrip("/")
+
+
+async def request(method, path, **kwargs):
+    """Fail transport errors instead of converting environment failures into rewards."""
+    # The synthetic slow-task tail can hold a session-open request for minutes;
+    # keep a generous timeout so it is not mistaken for an environment failure.
+    timeout = float(os.environ.get("ALFWORLD_HTTP_TIMEOUT", "600"))
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=server_url(), timeout=timeout, trust_env=False) as client:
+        response = await client.request(method, path, **kwargs)
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return response.json()
+
+
+def observation(state):
+    """Expose observations and legal actions, never the expert plan."""
+    return state["observation"] + "\nAvailable actions: " + "; ".join(state["commands"])
+
+
+class AlfworldTool(BaseTool):
+    """A tool call borrows a session; the agent loop owns its complete lifetime."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        schema = OpenAIFunctionToolSchema.model_validate(
+            {
+                "type": "function",
+                "function": {
+                    "name": "alfworld",
+                    "description": "Execute one ALFWorld action.",
+                    "parameters": {
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {
+                            "action": {
+                                "type": "string",
+                                "description": "An available action, copied exactly from the observation.",
+                            }
+                        },
+                        "required": ["action"],
+                    },
+                },
+            }
+        )
+        super().__init__({}, schema)
+
+    async def create(self, **kwargs):
+        """Reuse this trajectory's environment instead of resetting it per action."""
+        return kwargs["create_kwargs"]["session_id"], ToolResponse()
+
+    async def execute(self, instance_id, parameters, **kwargs):
+        """Step the environment and retain terminal status for the agent loop."""
+        agent_data = kwargs["agent_data"]
+        action = parameters.get("action")
+        if not isinstance(action, str) or not action:
+            return ToolResponse(text="Provide a nonempty action string."), 0.0, {}
+        try:
+            state = await request("POST", f"/sessions/{instance_id}/step", json={"action": action})
+        except Exception:
+            agent_data.extra_fields["alfworld_environment_error"] = True
+            raise
+        agent_data.extra_fields["alfworld_done"] = state["done"]
+        return ToolResponse(text=observation(state)), float(state["won"]), {}
+
+    async def release(self, instance_id, **kwargs):
+        """Per-call release must not destroy the episode owned by run()."""
+
+
+class AlfworldAgentLoop(ToolAgentLoop):
+    """One model-driven multi-turn episode, one final trajectory, binary environment reward."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, tools=None, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, tools=ToolListWrap([AlfworldTool()]), **kwargs)
+        if self.max_parallel_calls != 1:
+            raise ValueError("ALFWorld requires max_parallel_calls=1")
+
+    async def _handle_processing_tools_state(self, agent_data):
+        state = await super()._handle_processing_tools_state(agent_data)
+        if agent_data.extra_fields.get("alfworld_environment_error"):
+            raise RuntimeError("ALFWorld environment failed; discard the entire RL batch")
+        return AgentState.TERMINATED if agent_data.extra_fields.get("alfworld_done") else state
+
+    async def run(self, sampling_params, priority=0, **kwargs):
+        """Keep environment state alive through all tool calls and close it on failure."""
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        game_file = kwargs["extra_info"]["game_file"]
+        state = await request("POST", "/sessions", json={"game_file": game_file})
+        session_id = state["session_id"]
+        try:
+            kwargs["raw_prompt"] = list(kwargs["raw_prompt"]) + [{"role": "user", "content": observation(state)}]
+            kwargs["tools_kwargs"] = {"alfworld": {"create_kwargs": {"session_id": session_id}}}
+            output = await super().run(sampling_params, priority=priority, **kwargs)
+            state = await request("GET", f"/sessions/{session_id}")
+            if state.get("error") or output.extra_fields.get("alfworld_environment_error"):
+                raise RuntimeError("ALFWorld environment failed")
+            output.reward_score = float(state["won"])
+            record = dict(
+                game_file=game_file,
+                uid=kwargs.get("uid"),
+                session=kwargs.get("session_id"),
+                duration_s=time.monotonic() - started,
+                steps=state["steps"],
+                won=state["won"],
+                capped=state["steps"] >= state["max_steps"],
+                response_tokens=len(output.response_ids),
+                generated_tokens=sum(output.response_mask),
+            )
+            output.extra_fields["reward_extra_info"] = {"acc": output.reward_score, **record}
+            # Ray forwards worker stdout to the driver log; a bare logger.info can be
+            # dropped when the worker root handler level is WARNING. The pilot tooling
+            # parses these lines, so emit them on stdout as well.
+            record_line = "alfworld_episode " + json.dumps(record)
+            logger.info("%s", record_line)
+            print(record_line, flush=True)
+            return output
+        finally:
+            await request("DELETE", f"/sessions/{session_id}")

+"""CPU-only ALFWorld environment service; install in its own Python environment.
+
+Run: ALFWORLD_DATA=/data/alfworld python examples/group_delivery/alfworld_server.py
+The default bind address is loopback. Use a single server worker because sessions are local.
+"""
+
+import hashlib
+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
+from pathlib import Path
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+# Synthetic tail: real agentic workloads mix fast tasks with a small fraction
+# of very slow ones; ALFWorld's own spread is only ~1.3x (P95/P50), which never
+# exercises group_delivery's overlap. These knobs inject a deterministic
+# per-task tool latency (same task -> same delay in every run and every mode),
+# changing wall-clock time only, never the environment dynamics or rewards.
+TAIL_FRACTION = float(os.environ.get("ALFWORLD_TAIL_FRACTION", "0") or 0)
+TAIL_DELAY_MS = int(os.environ.get("ALFWORLD_TAIL_DELAY_MS", "0") or 0)
+
+
+def tail_delay_s(game_file: str) -> float:
+    """Deterministic slow-task delay from the game file hash (0 for fast tasks)."""
+    if TAIL_FRACTION <= 0 or TAIL_DELAY_MS <= 0:
+        return 0.0
+    digest = int(hashlib.sha1(game_file.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
+    if (digest % 1000) >= TAIL_FRACTION * 1000:
+        return 0.0
+    # +-20% jitter so the tail is a distribution, not a single spike.
+    jitter = 0.8 + 0.4 * ((digest >> 20) % 1000) / 1000.0
+    return TAIL_DELAY_MS * jitter / 1000.0
+
+
+def make_environment(game_file, max_steps):
+    """Construct the official text environment without privileged expert observations."""
+    import textworld
+    import textworld.gym
+    from alfworld.agents.environment.alfred_tw_env import AlfredDemangler, AlfredInfos
+
+    infos = textworld.EnvInfos(won=True, admissible_commands=True, extras=["gamefile"])
+    env_id = textworld.gym.register_games(
+        [str(game_file)],
+        infos,
+        batch_size=1,
+        asynchronous=False,
+        max_episode_steps=max_steps,
+        wrappers=[AlfredDemangler(shuffle=False), AlfredInfos],
+    )
+    return textworld.gym.make(env_id)
+
+
+class OpenSession(BaseModel):
+    """Path relative to ALFWORLD_DATA, supplied by the prepared dataset."""
+
+    game_file: str
+
+
+class Action(BaseModel):
+    """One environment action; model text never controls the reward."""
+
+    action: str
+
+
+def create_app(data_root, max_steps=50, environment_factory=make_environment):
+    """Create isolated sessions; an injectable factory allows CPU lifecycle tests."""
+    root = Path(data_root).resolve()
+    sessions, registry_lock = {}, threading.RLock()
+    # TextWorld's shared TatSu parser is not thread-safe; concurrent env.step()
+    # calls corrupt its grammar stack. FastAPI runs sync endpoints in a thread
+    # pool, so all environment access must be serialized process-wide.
+    env_lock = threading.RLock()
+
+    @asynccontextmanager
+    async def lifespan(app):
+        yield
+        with env_lock:
+            for session in sessions.values():
+                session["env"].close()
+
+    app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
+
+    def view(session):
+        return {key: value for key, value in session.items() if key not in ("env", "lock")}
+
+    def lookup(session_id):
+        with registry_lock:
+            if session_id not in sessions:
+                raise HTTPException(404, "Unknown environment session")
+            return sessions[session_id]
+
+    @app.post("/sessions")
+    def open_session(body: OpenSession):
+        path = (root / body.game_file).resolve()
+        if not path.is_relative_to(root) or path.name != "game.tw-pddl" or not path.is_file():
+            raise HTTPException(400, "Expected a game.tw-pddl file inside ALFWORLD_DATA")
+        # Sleep before taking registry_lock/env_lock: a slow task must not
+        # serialize session creation for every other concurrent episode.
+        delay_s = tail_delay_s(body.game_file)
+        if delay_s:
+            time.sleep(delay_s)
+        with registry_lock:
+            if len(sessions) >= 128:
+                raise HTTPException(503, "Too many active environment sessions")
+            env = environment_factory(path, max_steps)
+            try:
+                with env_lock:
+                    observations, infos = env.reset()
+            except Exception:
+                env.close()
+                raise
+            session_id = uuid4().hex
+            sessions[session_id] = dict(
+                env=env,
+                lock=threading.RLock(),
+                session_id=session_id,
+                observation=observations[0],
+                commands=list(infos["admissible_commands"][0]),
+                steps=0,
+                max_steps=max_steps,
+                won=False,
+                done=False,
+                error=False,
+            )
+            return view(sessions[session_id])
+
+    @app.get("/sessions/{session_id}")
+    def get_session(session_id: str):
+        session = lookup(session_id)
+        with session["lock"]:
+            return view(session)
+
+    @app.post("/sessions/{session_id}/step")
+    def step_session(session_id: str, body: Action):
+        session = lookup(session_id)
+        with session["lock"]:
+            if not session["done"]:
+                try:
+                    with env_lock:
+                        observations, _, dones, infos = session["env"].step([body.action])
+                    session.update(
+                        observation=observations[0],
+                        commands=list(infos["admissible_commands"][0]),
+                        won=bool(infos["won"][0]),
+                        steps=session["steps"] + 1,
+                    )
+                    session["done"] = bool(dones[0]) or session["won"] or session["steps"] >= max_steps
+                except Exception:
+                    session.update(error=True, done=True)
+                    raise
+            return view(session)
+
+    @app.delete("/sessions/{session_id}")
+    def close_session(session_id: str):
+        with registry_lock:
+            session = sessions.pop(session_id, None)
+        if session is not None:
+            with session["lock"]:
+                with env_lock:
+                    session["env"].close()
+        return {"closed": True}
+
+    return app
+
+

+        host="127.0.0.1",
+        port=8765,
+    )

+"""Prepare real ALFWorld tasks and optionally freeze a measured long-tail workload."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+
+SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
+    "Solve the household task in ALFWorld. Use the alfworld tool with exactly one available action per turn. "
+    "Explore locations and inspect receptacles as needed. Do not invent objects or claim success yourself. "
+    "The environment determines success. Keep reasoning brief and continue until the task is complete."
+)
+
+
+def episode_records(log_path):
+    """Read structured episode records from Ray's prefixed console logs."""
+    records = []
+    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
+    for line in Path(log_path).read_text().splitlines():
+        if "alfworld_episode " in line:
+            record, _ = decoder.raw_decode(line.split("alfworld_episode ", 1)[1])
+            records.append(record)
+    return records
+
+
+def group_durations(records, responses_per_group=2):
+    """Exclude incomplete groups and deduplicate replayed log lines."""
+    groups = defaultdict(dict)
+    for record in records:
+        groups[record["uid"]][record["session"]] = record
+    completed = []
+    for sessions in groups.values():
+        if set(sessions) != set(range(responses_per_group)):
+            continue
+        values = list(sessions.values())
+        if len({record["game_file"] for record in values}) != 1:
+            raise ValueError("A pilot group contains different games")
+        completed.append((values[0]["game_file"], max(record["duration_s"] for record in values)))
+    if not completed:
+        raise ValueError("No complete groups in pilot log; use rollout.val_kwargs.n=2")
+    return completed
+
+
+def tail_report(completed):
+    """Report measured group latency; the threshold is a workload criterion, not a dataset claim."""
+    durations = np.asarray([duration for _, duration in completed])
+    p50, p90, p95, p99 = np.percentile(durations, [50, 90, 95, 99])
+    return dict(
+        groups=len(completed),
+        p50_s=float(p50),
+        p90_s=float(p90),
+        p95_s=float(p95),
+        p99_s=float(p99),
+        max_s=float(durations.max()),
+        p95_over_p50=float(p95 / max(p50, 1e-9)),
+    )
+
+
+def select_long_tail(rows, completed, count, seed, minimum_ratio=5.0):
+    """Freeze an 80:20 fast/slow mixture using genuine measured training episodes."""
+    by_game = defaultdict(list)
+    available = {row["extra_info"]["game_file"]: row for row in rows}
+    for game, duration in completed:
+        if game in available:
+            by_game[game].append(duration)
+    medians = {game: float(np.median(values)) for game, values in by_game.items()}
+    if len(medians) < 32:
+        raise ValueError("Measure at least 32 distinct training games before selecting a tail subset")
+    ordered = sorted(medians, key=medians.get)
+    fast = ordered[: max(1, len(ordered) // 2)]
+    slow = ordered[-max(1, len(ordered) // 10) :]
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
+    slow_count = max(1, round(count * 0.2))
+    selected = list(rng.choice(fast, count - slow_count)) + list(rng.choice(slow, slow_count))
+    rng.shuffle(selected)
+    report = tail_report([(game, medians[game]) for game in selected])
+    if report["p95_over_p50"] < minimum_ratio:
+        raise ValueError(f"Measured mixture is not sufficiently long-tailed: {report}; collect a broader pilot")
+    return [available[game] for game in selected], report
+
+
+def collect_games(root, split):
+    """Use the official solvability filter and supported ALFWorld task families."""
+    rows = []
+    for game in sorted((root / "json_2.1.1" / split).rglob("game.tw-pddl")):
+        if "movable" in str(game) or "Sliced" in str(game):
+            continue
+        if not json.loads(game.read_text()).get("solvable", False):
+            continue
+        metadata = json.loads(game.with_name("traj_data.json").read_text())
+        rows.append(
+            dict(
+                data_source="alfworld",
+                agent_name="alfworld_agent",
+                ability="agentic_household",
+                prompt=[{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}],
+                reward_model={"style": "rule", "ground_truth": "environment_won"},
+                extra_info={
+                    "game_file": str(game.relative_to(root)),
+                    "task_type": metadata["task_type"],
+                    "split": split,
+                    "index": len(rows),
+                },
+            )
+        )

+"""Real Megatron fixed-batch vs group-delivery updates; requires CUDA and the megatron extra.
+
+Run with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 pytest -q -s tests/models/test_group_delivery_megatron.py.
+Larger topology cases skip when there are not enough visible GPUs. No model download is needed.
+"""
+
+import math
+from functools import partial
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.multiprocessing as mp
+
+TOPOLOGIES = [
+    (2, 1, 1, 1),
+    (1, 2, 1, 1),
+    (1, 1, 2, 1),
+    (1, 1, 1, 2),
+    (4, 1, 1, 1),
+    (2, 2, 1, 1),
+    (1, 2, 2, 1),
+    (1, 2, 2, 2),
+]
+
+
+def _make_model(path):
+    from transformers import Qwen3Config, Qwen3ForCausalLM
+
+    torch.manual_seed(19)
+    config = Qwen3Config(
+        vocab_size=128,
+        hidden_size=128,
+        intermediate_size=256,
+        num_hidden_layers=4,
+        num_attention_heads=4,
+        num_key_value_heads=2,
+        head_dim=32,
+        max_position_embeddings=256,
+        attention_dropout=0.0,
+        tie_word_embeddings=True,
+        bos_token_id=1,
+        eos_token_id=2,
+        pad_token_id=0,
+    )
+    Qwen3ForCausalLM(config).save_pretrained(path)
+
+
+def _batch(rows, dp_rank, dp_size, mode, group_id=None):
+    from tensordict import TensorDict
+
+    from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
+    from verl.workers.utils.padding import left_right_2_no_padding
+
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(23)
+    tokens = torch.randint(3, 128, (6, 64), generator=generator)
+    lengths = torch.tensor([4, 8, 15, 23, 8, 31])
+    rows = list(rows)
+    # Include real zero-loss DP lanes when rollout.n < DP.
+    padded = rows + [-1] * (-len(rows) % dp_size)
+    local = padded[dp_rank * (len(padded) // dp_size) : (dp_rank + 1) * (len(padded) // dp_size)]
+    ids = torch.stack([tokens[max(row, 0)] for row in local])
+    mask = torch.stack([torch.arange(32) < (lengths[row] if row >= 0 else 0) for row in local]).long()
+    attention = torch.cat([torch.ones_like(mask), mask], dim=1)
+    advantages = torch.tensor([(-1.0 if row % 2 == 0 else 1.0) if row >= 0 else 0.0 for row in local])
+    data = TensorDict(
+        dict(
+            input_ids=ids,
+            prompts=ids[:, :32],
+            responses=ids[:, 32:],
+            attention_mask=attention,
+            position_ids=torch.arange(64).expand(len(local), -1),
+            response_mask=mask,
+            old_log_probs=torch.full_like(mask, -math.log(128), dtype=torch.float32),
+            advantages=advantages[:, None].expand(-1, 32),
+        ),
+        batch_size=len(local),
+    ).to("cuda")
+    data = left_right_2_no_padding(data)
+    weight = int(lengths[rows].sum()) if mode == "token-mean" else len(rows)
+    tu.assign_non_tensor(
+        data,
+        global_batch_size=len(rows),
+        temperature=1.0,
+        calculate_entropy=False,
+        group_delivery_id=group_id,
+        group_delivery_weight=weight,
+    )
+    return data
+
+
+def _run_rank(rank, world_size, topology, mode, streaming, root, rendezvous):
+    from verl.utils import tensordict_utils as tu
+    from verl.workers.config import ActorConfig, HFModelConfig, McoreEngineConfig, McoreOptimizerConfig
+    from verl.workers.engine import EngineRegistry
+    from verl.workers.engine_workers_group_delivery import GroupDeliveryTrainingWorker
+    from verl.workers.utils.losses import ppo_loss
+
+    torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
+    dist.init_process_group("nccl", rank=rank, world_size=world_size, init_method=f"file://{rendezvous}")
+    _, tp, pp, cp = topology
+    model = HFModelConfig(path=str(Path(root) / "model"), load_tokenizer=False, use_remove_padding=True)
+    model.tokenizer = SimpleNamespace(pad_token_id=0, eos_token_id=2)
+    engine_config = McoreEngineConfig(
+        tensor_model_parallel_size=tp,
+        pipeline_model_parallel_size=pp,
+        context_parallel_size=cp,
+        use_mbridge=True,
+        use_distributed_optimizer=True,
+        param_offload=False,
+        optimizer_offload=False,
+        use_dynamic_bsz=False,
+        micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1,
+        use_remove_padding=True,
+        use_fused_kernels=False,
+        sequence_parallel=tp > 1,
+    )
+    optimizer_config = McoreOptimizerConfig(lr=1e-3, lr_decay_steps=2, clip_grad=0.1)
+    engine = EngineRegistry.new(
+        model_type="language_model",
+        backend="megatron",
+        model_config=model,
+        engine_config=engine_config,
+        optimizer_config=optimizer_config,
+        checkpoint_config=None,
+    )
+    engine.initialize()
+    worker = object.__new__(GroupDeliveryTrainingWorker)
+    worker.engine, worker.engine_config = engine, engine_config
+    worker.optimizer_config, worker.model_config = optimizer_config, model
+    worker.device_name, worker.flops_counter = "cuda", None
+    actor_config = ActorConfig(strategy="megatron", ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1, loss_agg_mode=mode)
+    worker.loss_fn = partial(ppo_loss, config=actor_config)
+    snapshots = []
+    actual_step = engine.optimizer_step
+
+    def capture_step():
+        # Inspect owned FP32 shards, not non-owned positions left by reduce-scatter.
+        # This harness targets the repository's pinned Megatron-Core 0.19.2 interface.
+        optimizers = getattr(engine.optimizer, "chained_optimizers", [engine.optimizer])
+        parameters = []
+        for optimizer in optimizers:
+            optimizer._copy_model_grads_to_main_grads()
+            parameters.extend(p for group in optimizer.optimizer.param_groups for p in group["params"])
+        before = [p.detach().float().cpu().clone() for p in parameters]
+        grads = [p.grad.detach().float().cpu().clone() for p in parameters]
+        norm = actual_step()
+        updates = [p.detach().float().cpu() - old for p, old in zip(parameters, before, strict=True)]
+        snapshots.append(dict(gradients=grads, updates=updates, norm=float(norm)))
+        return norm
+
+    engine.optimizer_step = capture_step
+    dp_rank, dp_size = engine.get_data_parallel_rank(), engine.get_data_parallel_size()
+    # Two consecutive batches detect stale bucket state and accidental scheduler steps.
+    for step in range(2):
+        if streaming:
+            worker.begin_group_batch(["a", "b", "c"])
+            for group_index in (2, 0, 1):
+                uid = "abc"[group_index]
+                worker.backward_group(_batch([2 * group_index, 2 * group_index + 1], dp_rank, dp_size, mode, uid))
+                assert len(snapshots) == step
+            worker.finish_group_batch()
+        else:
+            worker.optimizer_zero_grad()
+            data = _batch(range(6), dp_rank, dp_size, mode)
+            tu.assign_non_tensor(data, return_model_output=False)
+            worker.forward_backward(data)
+            worker.optimizer_step()
+            engine.lr_scheduler_step()
+    torch.save(snapshots, Path(root) / f"{streaming}-{rank}.pt")
+    dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def _relative_error(actual, expected):
+    numerator = sum((a - b).double().square().sum() for a, b in zip(actual, expected, strict=True))
+    denominator = sum(b.double().square().sum() for b in expected)
+    assert denominator > 0, "This regression must exercise a nonzero gradient/update"
+    return float((numerator / denominator).sqrt())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topology", TOPOLOGIES, ids=[f"dp{d}-tp{t}-pp{p}-cp{c}" for d, t, p, c in TOPOLOGIES])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["token-mean", "seq-mean-token-mean"])
+def test_group_delivery_matches_full_batch_on_megatron(tmp_path, topology, mode):
+    world_size = math.prod(topology)
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.device_count() < world_size:
+        pytest.skip(f"Requires {world_size} CUDA GPUs")
+    # With CUDA present, missing Megatron is an installation failure, not a passing skip.
+    __import__("megatron.core")
+    _make_model(tmp_path / "model")
+    for streaming in (False, True):
+        mp.spawn(
+            _run_rank,
+            args=(world_size, topology, mode, streaming, str(tmp_path), str(tmp_path / f"rendezvous-{streaming}")),
+            nprocs=world_size,
+            join=True,
+        )
+    for rank in range(world_size):
+        baseline = torch.load(tmp_path / f"False-{rank}.pt", weights_only=True)
+        delivered = torch.load(tmp_path / f"True-{rank}.pt", weights_only=True)
+        assert len(baseline) == len(delivered) == 2
+        for expected, actual in zip(baseline, delivered, strict=True):
+            assert _relative_error(actual["gradients"], expected["gradients"]) < 0.02
+            assert _relative_error(actual["updates"], expected["updates"]) < 0.03
+            assert actual["norm"] == pytest.approx(expected["norm"], rel=0.02)

+class Environment:

+
+    def __init__(self, fail=False):
+        self.steps, self.closed, self.fail = 0, False, fail
+
+    def reset(self):
+        return ["initial"], {"admissible_commands": [["look"]]}
+
+    def step(self, actions):
+        if self.fail:
+            raise RuntimeError("environment crashed")
+        self.steps += 1
+        return (
+            [f"step {self.steps}"],
+            [0.0],
+            [self.steps == 2],
+            {"won": [self.steps == 2], "admissible_commands": [["look"]]},
+        )
+
+    def close(self):

+            data = SimpleNamespace(extra_fields={})

+                metrics={},

+class FinalizingEngine:
+    """CPU stand-in whose finalization would corrupt gradients carried across calls."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.grad = torch.zeros(3)
+        self.module = [SimpleNamespace(buffers=[SimpleNamespace(grad_data=self.grad)])]
+        self.optimizer = SimpleNamespace(config=SimpleNamespace(optimizer="adam"))
+        self.tf_config = SimpleNamespace()
+        self.steps = self.schedules = 0
+        self.applied = None
+        self.fail = False
+        self.retain_output = None
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def train_mode(self, zero_grad_on_exit=True, **kwargs):
+        """Mirror the native engine's gradient lifetime."""
+        try:
+            yield
+        finally:
+            if zero_grad_on_exit:
+                self.optimizer_zero_grad()
+
+    def optimizer_zero_grad(self):
+        """Reset native schedule buffers."""
+        self.grad.zero_()
+
+    def forward_backward_batch(self, data, **kwargs):
+        """Finalize each group; previous gradients must already have been removed."""
+        assert not self.grad.any()
+        self.retain_output = tu.get(data, "return_model_output")
+        self.grad.add_(data["gradient"][0]).mul_(2)
+        if self.fail:
+            raise RuntimeError("engine backward failed")
+        return {"model_output": {"log_probs": torch.zeros(1)}, "loss": [1.0], "metrics": {}}
+
+    def optimizer_step(self):
+        """Capture the final gradient received by the optimizer."""
+        self.steps += 1
+        self.applied = self.grad.clone()
+        return self.grad.norm().item()
+
+    def lr_scheduler_step(self):
+        """Count updates independently from backward calls."""
+        self.schedules += 1

+"""Numerical equivalence to a full-batch GRPO update, including unequal response lengths."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace

+import pytest

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["token-mean", "seq-mean-token-mean", "seq-mean-token-sum", "seq-mean-token-sum-norm"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("order", [(0, 1, 2), (2, 0, 1)])
+def test_streaming_matches_full_batch_gradient_and_adam_update(mode, order):
+    torch.manual_seed(17)
+    features = torch.randn(6, 7, 5)
+    masks = torch.arange(7)[None, :] < torch.tensor([1, 2, 7, 6, 2, 4])[:, None]
+    # Three two-response GRPO groups, rewards differ only within the group.
+    rewards = torch.tensor([0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, -1.0, 3.0]).reshape(3, 2)
+    advantages = ((rewards - rewards.mean(1, keepdim=True)) / rewards.std(1, keepdim=True)).flatten()
+    initial = torch.randn(5) * 0.05
+    reference = torch.nn.Parameter(initial.clone())
+    streaming = torch.nn.Parameter(initial.clone())
+    old_log_probs = features @ initial + 0.1 * torch.randn(6, 7)
+
+    def loss(parameter, rows):
+        log_probs = features[rows] @ parameter
+        ratio = (log_probs - old_log_probs[rows]).exp()
+        adv = advantages[rows, None]
+        clipped = torch.maximum(-adv * ratio, -adv * ratio.clamp(0.8, 1.2))
+        # An additional KL-like term shares the configured RL normalizer.
+        terms = clipped + 0.02 * log_probs.square()
+        mask = masks[rows]
+        if mode == "token-mean":
+            return (terms * mask).sum() / mask.sum(), mask.sum().item()
+        sequence_losses = (terms * mask).sum(-1)
+        if mode == "seq-mean-token-mean":
+            sequence_losses = sequence_losses / mask.sum(-1)
+        if mode == "seq-mean-token-sum-norm":
+            sequence_losses = sequence_losses / 7
+        return sequence_losses.mean(), len(rows)
+
+    reference_optim = torch.optim.AdamW([reference], lr=0.01)
+    streaming_optim = torch.optim.AdamW([streaming], lr=0.01)
+    loss(reference, list(range(6)))[0].backward()
+    reference_gradient = reference.grad.clone()
+    expected_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_([reference], 0.2)
+    reference_optim.step()
+
+    accumulator = GroupGradientAccumulator([str(i) for i in order])
+    buffer = torch.zeros_like(streaming)
+    for i in order:
+        streaming_optim.zero_grad()
+        group_loss, weight = loss(streaming, [2 * i, 2 * i + 1])
+        group_loss.backward()
+        buffer.copy_(streaming.grad)
+        accumulator.add(str(i), {"buffer": buffer}, weight)
+        # Model/optimizer stay unchanged; engine buffers can be reused immediately.
+        buffer.zero_()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(streaming, initial, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        assert len(streaming_optim.state) == 0
+    accumulator.restore({"buffer": buffer})
+    torch.testing.assert_close(buffer, reference_gradient, rtol=2e-6, atol=2e-7)
+    streaming.grad = buffer
+    actual_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_([streaming], 0.2)
+    streaming_optim.step()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_norm, expected_norm)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(streaming, reference, rtol=2e-6, atol=2e-7)

+"""Fixed-batch sampling for synchronous, group-streamed GRPO."""
+
+import time
+
+from verl.trainer.ppo.v1.replay_buffer import ReplayBuffer
+
+
+class GroupDeliveryReplayBuffer(ReplayBuffer):
+    """Deliver complete groups from exactly one fixed batch, without refill or dropping."""
+
+    def begin_batch(self, group_ids: list[str], global_steps: int, responses_per_group: int) -> None:
+        """Record the identities and version of the batch before dispatching rollout."""
+        if getattr(self, "remaining", None):
+            raise RuntimeError("The previous group batch is incomplete")
+        if not group_ids or len(set(group_ids)) != len(group_ids):
+            raise ValueError("A synchronous batch requires unique group IDs")
+        self.remaining = set(group_ids)
+        self.batch_step = global_steps
+        self.responses_per_group = responses_per_group
+
+    def sample(self, global_steps: int, partition_id: str, batch_size: int):
+        """Wait for any complete group; fail the whole batch if a sibling fails."""
+        if partition_id != "train":
+            return super().sample(global_steps, partition_id, batch_size)
+        if batch_size != 1 or not getattr(self, "remaining", None) or global_steps != self.batch_step:
+            raise ValueError("Group streaming must consume one group from the active synchronous batch")
+        while True:
+            self._sync_metadata_from_transfer_queue()
+            versions = self.prompt_global_steps[partition_id]
+            if set(versions) != self.remaining or any(step != global_steps for step in versions.values()):
+                raise RuntimeError("TransferQueue contains missing, foreign, or wrong-version prompt groups")
+            if self.failure_keys[partition_id]:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Rollout failed for synchronous groups: {sorted(self.failure_keys[partition_id])}")
+            ready = self.finished_keys[partition_id] & self.remaining
+            wait_for_all = self.trainer_config.get("wait_for_full_batch", False)
+            if ready and (not wait_for_all or ready == self.remaining):
+                uid = sorted(ready)[0]
+                trajectories = {
+                    key: tag for key, tag in self.partitions[partition_id].items() if key.split("_", 1)[0] == uid
+                }
+                expected = {f"{uid}_{session}_0" for session in range(self.responses_per_group)}
+                if set(trajectories) != expected:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"Group {uid} must have exactly one trajectory for each of {self.responses_per_group} sessions"
+                    )
+                for tag in trajectories.values():
+                    if (
+                        tag.get("global_steps") != global_steps
+                        or tag.get("min_global_steps") != global_steps - 1
+                        or tag.get("max_global_steps") != global_steps - 1
+                    ):
+                        raise RuntimeError(f"Group {uid} contains stale or cross-version trajectories")
+                batch = self._materialize_batch(partition_id, [uid], trajectories)
+                batch.extra_info["group_delivery_id"] = uid
+                self.remaining.remove(uid)
+                return batch, {}
+            time.sleep(self.poll_interval)
+
+    def finish_batch(self) -> None:
+        """Check the barrier before committing an optimizer update."""
+        if getattr(self, "remaining", None):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Still waiting for {len(self.remaining)} prompt groups")

+def validate_group_delivery_config(config: DictConfig) -> None:
+    """Reject features that change the fixed-batch objective or update boundary."""
+    actor = config.actor_rollout_ref.actor
+    rollout = config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
+    conditions = {
+        "actor.strategy=megatron": actor.strategy == "megatron",
+        "actor_rollout_ref.hybrid_engine=False": not config.actor_rollout_ref.hybrid_engine,
+        "dedicated rollout GPUs": rollout.nnodes > 0 and rollout.n_gpus_per_node > 0,
+        "a distributed checkpoint engine": rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend != "naive",
+        "algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo": config.algorithm.adv_estimator == "grpo",
+        "rollout.n > 1": rollout.n > 1,
+        "actor.ppo_epochs=1": actor.ppo_epochs == 1,
+        "actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=data.train_batch_size": actor.ppo_mini_batch_size == config.data.train_batch_size,
+        "actor.policy_loss.loss_mode=vanilla": actor.policy_loss.loss_mode == "vanilla",
+        "no critic": not need_critic(config),
+        "no distillation": not is_distillation_enabled(config.get("distillation")),
+        "algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False (KL loss is supported)": not config.algorithm.use_kl_in_reward,
+        "no dynamic group filtering": not OmegaConf.select(config, "algorithm.filter_groups.enable", default=False),
+        "no rollout skipping": not OmegaConf.select(config, "skip.rollout_tq.enable", default=False),
+        "no custom sampler": not OmegaConf.select(config, "trainer.v1.sampler.custom_sampler.path"),
+        "no score centering": not OmegaConf.select(
+            config, "algorithm.rollout_correction.score_centering", default=False
+        ),
+        "no batch-dependent rollout correction": not (
+            OmegaConf.select(config, "algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is")
+            or OmegaConf.select(config, "algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_rs")
+        ),
+        "no actor score centering": not OmegaConf.select(
+            config, "actor_rollout_ref.actor.policy_loss.rollout_correction.score_centering", default=False
+        ),
+        "no actor warmup": config.trainer.critic_warmup == 0,
+        "positive polling interval": config.trainer.v1.group_delivery.poll_interval > 0,
+        "positive train batch": config.data.train_batch_size > 0,
+    }
+    reward_model = config.reward.reward_model
+    conditions["a separate reward model pool"] = not reward_model.enable or reward_model.enable_resource_pool
+    supported_losses = {"token-mean", "seq-mean-token-mean", "seq-mean-token-sum", "seq-mean-token-sum-norm"}
+    conditions["a supported mean loss aggregation"] = actor.loss_agg_mode in supported_losses
+    if actor.loss_agg_mode == "seq-mean-token-sum-norm":
+        conditions["a positive fixed actor.loss_scale_factor"] = (
+            actor.loss_scale_factor is not None and actor.loss_scale_factor > 0
+        )
+    failed = [description for description, ok in conditions.items() if not ok]
+    if failed:
+        raise ValueError("group_delivery requires: " + "; ".join(failed))

+@register_trainer("group_delivery")
+class PPOTrainerGroupDelivery(PPOTrainerSeparateAsync):
+    """Reuse standalone resource setup, with no prefetch, partial rollout, or early updates.
+
+    Each controller iteration delivers one complete GRPO group to all actor ranks.
+    Padding satisfies DP dispatch; the worker stores already finalized gradients
+    outside Megatron's schedule buffers. The last group opens the optimizer barrier.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, config: DictConfig):
+        validate_group_delivery_config(config)
+        self._enable_hybrid_replicas = False
+        # Deliberately bypass the async initializer and all switching/prefetch state.
+        PPOTrainer.__init__(self, config)
+
+    def _build_replay_buffer(self):
+        return GroupDeliveryReplayBuffer(
+            trainer_mode="group_delivery",
+            trainer_config=self.config.trainer.v1.group_delivery,
+            max_off_policy_threshold=None,
+            max_off_policy_strategy="drop",
+            sampler_kwargs={},
+            poll_interval=self.config.trainer.v1.group_delivery.poll_interval,
+        )
+
+    def _init_resource_pool_mgr(self):
+        PPOTrainer._init_resource_pool_mgr(self)
+        self.role_worker_mapping[Role.Actor] = ray.remote(GroupDeliveryActorWorker)
+
+    def get_llm_client(self):
+        return self.standalone_server_manager.get_client(client_cls=LLMServerClient)
+
+    def _reissue_inflight_prompts(self, partition_id="train") -> int:
+        # Checkpoints are only taken after the accumulation window was committed.
+        # A restored async checkpoint with pending prompts has different semantics.
+        partitions = tq.kv_list(partition_id) or {}
+        tags = partitions.get(partition_id, {})
+        if any(tag.get("is_prompt", False) for tag in tags.values()):
+            raise RuntimeError("group_delivery cannot resume a checkpoint containing unconsumed prompt groups")
+        if tags:
+            tq.kv_clear(keys=list(tags), partition_id=partition_id)
+        return 0
+
+    def on_init_end(self):
+        # The dedicated rollout replicas are created with load_format=dummy and
+        # hold no checkpoint weights; publish them before the first rollout.
+        self.standalone_checkpoint_manager.update_weights(self.global_steps)
+
+    def on_train_begin(self):
+        """No warmup or next-step prompts may run under the current policy."""
+
+    def on_step_begin(self):
+        """The fixed batch is submitted by step(), after opening the gradient window."""
+
+    def on_validate_begin(self):
+        """Dedicated rollout replicas are already available for validation."""
+
+    def on_sample_begin(self):
+        """Rollout continues while the actor consumes completed groups."""
+
+    def on_sample_end(self):
+        """Keep rollout replicas running until the fixed batch finishes."""
+
+    def _record_event(self, event: str, **details) -> None:
+        """Emit controller timestamps for overlap and update-boundary verification."""
+        logger.info(
+            "group_delivery_event %s",
+            json.dumps(dict(event=event, step=self.global_steps, monotonic_s=time.monotonic(), **details)),
+        )
+
+    def on_step_end(self):
+        with marked_timer("update_weights", self.timing_raw, color="red"):
+            self._record_event("weight_sync_begin")
+            self._pending_sync_metrics = self.standalone_checkpoint_manager.update_weights(self.global_steps)
+            self._record_event("weight_sync_end")
+
+    def _compute_old_log_prob(self, batch, metrics):
+        # Actor parameters remain unchanged throughout the entire batch.
+        return PPOTrainer._compute_old_log_prob(self, batch, metrics)
+
+    def _get_required_batch_multiple(self, dp_size: int) -> int:
+        # There is no optimizer mini-batch inside a group. Only align to DP here;
+        # the engine owns token packing and PP/VPP micro-batch alignment.
+        actor = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor
+        multiple = dp_size
+        if not actor.use_dynamic_bsz:
+            multiple = math.lcm(multiple, dp_size * actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu)
+        rollout = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout
+        if not rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz:
+            multiple = math.lcm(multiple, dp_size * rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu)
+        if self.use_reference_policy:
+            ref = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.ref
+            ref_dp = dp_size
+            if not self.ref_in_actor:
+                wg = self.ref_policy_wg
+                if "ref" not in wg._dispatch_info:
+                    wg._dispatch_info["ref"] = wg._query_dispatch_info("ref")
+                ref_dp = max(wg._dispatch_info["ref"]) + 1
+            multiple = math.lcm(multiple, ref_dp)
+            if not ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz:
+                multiple = math.lcm(multiple, ref_dp * ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu)
+        return multiple
+
+    def step(self, metrics: dict, timing_raw: dict) -> KVBatchMeta:
+        prompts = self._next_train_batch()
+        group_ids = list(prompts["uid"])
+        if "__rollout_n__" in prompts.keys():
+            raise ValueError("group_delivery requires the configured, fixed rollout.n for every prompt")
+        self.replay_buffer.begin_batch(group_ids, self.global_steps, self.config.actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n)
+        keys, tags = [], []
+        aggregator = MetricsAggregator()
+        self._overlapped_groups = 0
+        self._record_event("batch_begin", groups=len(group_ids))
+        try:
+            self.actor_rollout_wg.begin_group_batch(group_ids)
+            self._submit_batch_to_rollout(prompts)
+            for _ in group_ids:
+                group_metrics = {}
+                batch = self._step_once(group_metrics, timing_raw, sample_batch_size=1)
+                keys.extend(batch.keys)
+                tags.extend(batch.tags)
+                aggregator.add_step_metrics(group_metrics, sample_count=int(batch.extra_info["group_delivery_weight"]))
+            self.replay_buffer.finish_batch()
+            with marked_timer("optimizer_step", timing_raw, color="red"):
+                self._record_event("optimizer_begin")
+                results = self.actor_rollout_wg.finish_group_batch()
+                self._record_event("optimizer_end")
+        except Exception:
+            # Log the original failure before touching the workers: if one rank
+            # died inside a collective (e.g. a CUDA OOM), its peer spins there
+            # and any cleanup RPC to that peer never returns. Without this line
+            # the traceback is lost behind the blocked cleanup.
+            logger.exception("group_delivery step failed; aborting the batch")
+            # Both cleanups must be attempted; preserve the original failure.
+            cleanups = (
+                ("abort_group_batch", self.actor_rollout_wg.abort_group_batch),
+                ("abort_replicas", self.standalone_checkpoint_manager.abort_replicas),
+            )
+            for name, cleanup in cleanups:
+                executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
+                try:
+                    executor.submit(cleanup).result(timeout=60)
+                except TimeoutError:
+                    logger.exception("group_delivery cleanup %s timed out; worker is stuck", name)
+                except Exception:
+                    logger.exception("group_delivery cleanup %s failed", name)
+                finally:
+                    executor.shutdown(wait=False)
+            raise
+        metrics.update(aggregator.get_aggregated_metrics())
+        # ONE_TO_ALL returns one result per rank; the optimizer computes a global norm.
+        # PP rank zero need not own outputs; pick each metric from its first output rank.
+        for result in results:
+            for key, value in result.items():
+                if value is not None:
+                    metrics.setdefault(f"actor/{key}", value)
+        metrics["training/groups_backward_started_during_rollout"] = self._overlapped_groups
+        metrics["training/delivered_groups"] = len(group_ids)
+        metrics["training/optimizer_steps"] = 1
+        return KVBatchMeta(partition_id="train", keys=keys, tags=tags)
+
+    def _update_actor(self, batch: KVBatchMeta, metrics: dict) -> KVBatchMeta:
+        actor = self.config.actor_rollout_ref.actor
+        group_ids = {
+            key.split("_", 1)[0] for key, tag in zip(batch.keys, batch.tags, strict=True) if not tag.get("is_padding")
+        }

+"""Accumulate independently finalized group gradients without re-reducing old gradients."""
+
+import math
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+import torch
+
+
+class GroupGradientAccumulator:
+    """Weighted sum of group means, with an exact-once barrier before an optimizer step.
+
+    Megatron's schedule finalizes (and sometimes rescales) its gradient buffers on
+    every call. Keep the running sum outside those buffers, zero the engine before
+    each group, and restore the sum only after the entire synchronous batch arrives.
+    Weights are valid response-token counts for token-mean, or valid sequence counts
+    for sequence-mean. This uses one additional FP32 gradient buffer.
+
+    The running sum may live on a different device than the gradients (typically
+    host memory). On a full-parameter 4B/TP2 run the extra FP32 buffer is 8 GiB
+    of GPU that must sit next to main_grad for the entire backward, which leaves
+    no room for activations on a 48 GB card. Accumulating on CPU trades that
+    memory for one D2H copy of each group's gradient plus one H2D at step time,
+    while keeping the sum itself exactly FP32.
+    """
+
+    # Pinned staging buffer used to move one gradient chunk at a time when the
+    # sum is host-resident. Pageable D2H runs at ~2 GB/s on this host; pinned
+    # memory reaches ~10 GB/s, which is the difference between 20 s and 3 s per
+    # four-group step. The buffer is bounded so host pinning stays cheap.
+    STAGING_BYTES = 256 << 20
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        group_ids: list[str],
+        sums: dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
+        staging: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ):
+        if not group_ids or len(set(group_ids)) != len(group_ids):
+            raise ValueError("Expected a nonempty list of unique group IDs")
+        self.expected = frozenset(group_ids)
+        self.seen: set[str] = set()
+        # A caller may pass the same buffers back on every batch. Reusing one
+        # persistent FP32 buffer avoids a fresh ~4 bytes/owned-parameter
+        # allocation (7.5 GiB for 4B/TP2) in an already tight memory budget.
+        self.sums: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = sums if sums is not None else {}
+        for value in self.sums.values():
+            value.zero_()
+        self.weight = 0.0
+        self.restored = False
+        # A caller may also pass a persistent pinned staging buffer, so the
+        # (expensive) pin/unpin does not repeat on every batch.
+        self._staging: torch.Tensor | None = staging
+
+    def check_group(self, group_id: str, weight: float) -> None:
+        """Reject duplicate, foreign, or invalid groups before running backward."""
+        if self.restored or group_id not in self.expected or group_id in self.seen:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected or duplicate group: {group_id}")
+        if not math.isfinite(weight) or weight <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Group weight must be finite and positive, got {weight}")
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def add(self, group_id: str, gradients: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor], weight: float) -> None:
+        """Copy a group's already synchronized gradients into the running sum."""
+        self.check_group(group_id, weight)
+        if not gradients:
+            raise ValueError("No Megatron gradient buffers were found")
+        if self.sums and gradients.keys() != self.sums.keys():
+            raise ValueError("Gradient buffer layout changed within a synchronous batch")
+        for name, grad in gradients.items():
+            if grad.dtype != torch.float32:
+                raise ValueError("Group accumulation requires FP32 Megatron gradient buffers")
+            if name in self.sums and self.sums[name].shape != grad.shape:
+                raise ValueError(f"Gradient buffer changed within a synchronous batch: {name}")
+        for name, grad in gradients.items():
+            if name not in self.sums:
+                self.sums[name] = torch.zeros_like(grad)
+            target = self.sums[name]
+            if grad.device == target.device:
+                target.add_(grad, alpha=weight)
+            else:
+                # The sum may be host-resident (see class docstring); move this
+                # group's gradient chunk by chunk through pinned memory.
+                self._accumulate_host(target, grad, weight)
+        self.weight += weight
+        self.seen.add(group_id)
+
+    def _staging_for(self, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Return a pinned 1-D staging buffer matching ``tensor``'s dtype."""
+        if self._staging is None or self._staging.dtype != tensor.dtype:
+            elements = max(1, self.STAGING_BYTES // tensor.element_size())
+            self._staging = torch.empty(elements, dtype=tensor.dtype, pin_memory=True)
+        return self._staging
+
+    def _copy_chunked(self, destination: torch.Tensor, source: torch.Tensor, *, accumulate: bool, weight: float):
+        """Move ``source`` into ``destination`` across devices through pinned memory."""
+        staging = self._staging_for(source)
+        source_flat = source.reshape(-1)
+        destination_flat = destination.reshape(-1)
+        step = staging.numel()
+        for offset in range(0, destination_flat.numel(), step):
+            count = min(step, destination_flat.numel() - offset)
+            staging[:count].copy_(source_flat[offset : offset + count])
+            if accumulate:
+                destination_flat[offset : offset + count].add_(staging[:count], alpha=weight)
+            else:
+                destination_flat[offset : offset + count].copy_(staging[:count])
+
+    def _accumulate_host(self, target: torch.Tensor, grad: torch.Tensor, weight: float) -> None:
+        self._copy_chunked(target, grad, accumulate=True, weight=weight)
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def restore(self, gradients: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+        """Restore the global mean exactly once, before clipping and optimizer.step."""
+        if self.restored or self.seen != self.expected:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Cannot step: received {len(self.seen)}/{len(self.expected)} groups")
+        if gradients.keys() != self.sums.keys():
+            raise ValueError("Gradient buffer layout changed before optimizer step")
+        for name, grad in gradients.items():
+            if grad.shape != self.sums[name].shape:
+                raise ValueError(f"Gradient buffer changed before optimizer step: {name}")
+        for name, grad in gradients.items():
+            source = self.sums[name]
+            if grad.device == source.device:
+                grad.copy_(source)
+            else:
+                # One H2D per step, streamed through the pinned staging buffer.
+                self._copy_chunked(grad, source, accumulate=False, weight=0.0)
+            grad.div_(self.weight)
+        self.restored = True
+        # Keep self.sums: a caller may own these buffers and reuse them for the
+        # next batch. The next accumulator zeroes them in __init__; clearing the
+        # dict here would drop (and force reallocation of) a persistent buffer.
+
+
+def megatron_gradient_buffers(modules) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Return native DDP buffers, including expert buffers and distributed-optimizer shards.
+
+    Accumulating the physical grad_data storage preserves reduce-scatter results
+    even when a distributed optimizer owns only slices of individual parameters.
+    Megatron FSDP / precision-aware optimizer layouts are deliberately unsupported.
+    """
+    gradients = {}
+    seen = set()
+    for chunk_index, module in enumerate(modules):
+        for kind in ("buffers", "expert_parallel_buffers"):
+            for buffer_index, buffer in enumerate(getattr(module, kind, ())):
+                grad = buffer.grad_data
+                if id(grad) not in seen:
+                    gradients[f"{chunk_index}/{kind}/{buffer_index}"] = grad
+                    seen.add(id(grad))
+    if not gradients:
+        raise RuntimeError("group_delivery requires native Megatron DDP gradient buffers")
+    return gradients
